title: Continuous-function set coefficients and their scheme pullbacks
statement:
Let $D$ be a Hausdorff totally disconnected topological space, and write $\underline D(S)=C(S,D)$ on profinite sets with the topology generated by finite jointly surjective families. For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], let $p_X^*$ be the set-valued inverse image from this profinite site specified in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. On the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the presheaf
$$F_{D,X}(U)=C(|U|,D)$$
is a sheaf and is canonically isomorphic to $p_X^*\underline D$. This isomorphism is natural in continuous maps of spaces $D\to D'$ and respects finite products, including the one-point space. For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, the induced comparison
$$f^{-1}F_{D,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{D,Y}$$
for the actual inverse image on set sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is an isomorphism, compatible with identity and composition. If $D$ is discrete, $F_{D,X}$ is the associated constant set sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], composition with the quotient to connected components identifies $F_{D,X}(U)$ with $C(\pi_0(U),D)$. All sheaves and indexing categories use compatible universes.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6, the continuous-function realization argument with the ring operations omitted (an agent set-valued formulation); Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.2.12, p. 30, for the sheaf, discrete and component assertions. Scheme-pullback comparison uses the composition comparison of lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback.

proof.text: Restrict Mathlib's fpqc continuous-map sheaf along the small pro-etale forgetful functor, using that pro-etale coverings are fpqc. This proves continuousSetPresheaf_isSheaf before bundling continuousSetSheaf. The component formula is definitionally the inverse of Mathlib's connected-component factorization equivalence; the discrete comparison is the last clause of continuousSet_descent_components.

The normalized Kan-evaluation theorem gives a unique normalized morphism sigma and a bijection on every affine object weakly contractible for set sheaves. Convert the epimorphism-surjectivity property of the affine covering-family theorem into its locally-surjective definition of weak contractibility using Mathlib's equivalence between locally surjective set-sheaf maps and epimorphisms.

For an arbitrary object choose its affine weakly contractible covering. Every arrow of this cover lies in the equalizer sieve for two sections with equal sigma image, by injectivity on that affine and naturality. Every arrow likewise lies in the image sieve of any target section, by surjectivity on that affine. Their generated covering sieves therefore prove local injectivity and local surjectivity. Apply the set-sheaf local-bijection criterion to obtain IsIso sigma. The uniqueness already supplied by Kan evaluation proves unique existence with normalization and IsIso, and its specification proves continuousSetRealizationHom_spec.

Apply the normalized-comparison coherence theorem to continuousSetRealizationHom and its normalization specification. Project its coefficient, finite-product, scheme-square, identity and composition clauses, reversing the displayed equations where needed. In the scheme square, both normalized realization maps and the point comparison are isomorphisms, so IsIso.of_isIso_comp_left proves invertibility of the actual continuousSetPullbackMap. Its direct-image naturality prerequisite is proved directly by the first-projection identity for the base-change pullback map.
